examples.problem:
Given that the discrete random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ shown in the table below, compute $P(X=5).$

| $x$ | $1$ | $3$ | $5$ | $7$ | $9$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $F(x)$ | $0.15$ | $0.45$ | $0.50$ | $0.90$ | $1.0$ |
examples.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is the function $F(x)$ defined by

$$
F(x) = P(X \leq x).
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(5) & =P(X\le 5) \\  & =P(X\in {1,3,5}) \\  & =P(X=1)+P(X=3)+P(X=5) \\  & =P(X\in {1,3})+P(X=5) \\  & =P(X\le 3)+P(X=5) \\  & =F(3)+P(X=5).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=5) & =F(5)-F(3) \\  & =0.50-0.45 \\  & =0.05.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Given that the discrete random variable $Y$ has the probability mass function $f(y)$ (as shown in the table below) and the cumulative distribution function $F(y)$, compute $F(2)-F(1).$

| $y$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(y)$ | $0.343$ | $0.441$ | $0.189$ | $0.027$ |

$F(2)-F(1)=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $Y$ is a function $F(y)$ such that

$$
F(y)=P(Y\le y).
$$

Computing $F(1)$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}F(1) & =P(Y\le 1) \\  & =P(Y\in {0,1}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1) \\  & =0.343+0.441 \\  & =0.784.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $F(2)$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}F(2) & =P(Y\le 2) \\  & =P(Y\in {0,1,2}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1)+f(2) \\  & =0.343+0.441+0.189 \\  & =0.973.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
F(2)-F(1)=0.973-0.784=0.189
$$
